settings.accounts.intro: Every credential saved in this browser, and the local data each one owns. Use this to clean up duplicate logins, or to reset one account's local data without signing out of it.

settings.anonymous.intro: Control how the browser-local Anonymous home feed is assembled.
settings.anonymous.maxAge: Maximum age of posts from followed accounts
settings.anonymous.maxAge.hint: Older posts are left out when Anonymous builds Home. Posts from followed hashtags are not affected.
settings.anonymous.title: Anonymous
settings.appearance.expandSpoilers: Always expand posts marked with content warnings
settings.appearance.intro: Adjust how the web interface looks and behaves.
settings.appearance.title: Appearance
settings.content.everyone.hint: Applies to every post from every account, on this Mastodon account only. Stored in this browser — it is a reading preference, not something the server knows about.
settings.content.expandCw.note: Posts with a content warning render already open. The warning text is still shown above the post, so you always know one was set.
settings.content.flipside.after: : that page is for accounts you want less of, this one is for accounts you want without a doorway in front of them.
settings.content.footnote: Trust never overrides a filter. A word filter you set, or a post your server chose to hide, stays hidden — those are your rules and the server's, and one person being trusted is not a reason to break them.
settings.content.howFar.hint: One choice, so there is never a question of which setting wins. Whoever this covers, their content warnings open on their own and their sensitive media renders unblurred.
settings.content.independent: The switches above are what Mawkingbird itself obeys, and are independent of it.
settings.content.intro: A content warning is the author's judgement about their audience, not about you. For people you read all the time, clicking through the same warning every day is friction without safety — so you can switch it off, either for everyone or for specific people.
settings.content.keptNote: Nobody is added to your list by this. Your named accounts below are kept exactly as they are, so switching back to "individual people" finds them still there.
settings.content.level.follows.note: Including people you follow in future — this is checked as you read, not copied into a list, so it keeps up on its own. Boosts are still judged by whoever originally wrote them.
settings.content.level.followsBoosts: Trust everyone I follow, and what they boost
settings.content.level.followsBoosts.note: The widest setting. A boost from someone you follow opens the warning on the boosted post too, even though you may not follow — or know — whoever wrote it.
settings.content.level.individuals.note: Only the accounts you have named, listed further down. This is the default.
settings.content.level.none.note: Every warning and blur stays in place, including for accounts on the list below.
settings.content.onServer.after: . Mawkingbird can read it but not change it — Mastodon has no API for that, so it can only be set from your server's own settings page.
settings.content.onServer.before: Your Mastodon account has its own "always expand content warnings" preference, which other apps read. It is currently
settings.content.revoke.hint: Drops to "trust no one", turns both switches off, and forgets every account you have trusted. Unlike the choices above, this one throws the list away — there is no undo.
settings.content.revokedNote: These two are off while trust is revoked. Choose another level above to use them.
settings.content.showSensitive.note: Images and video flagged sensitive render without the blur.
settings.content.title: 🙈 Trust: CW/Sensitive
settings.content.trusted.before: People whose warnings and sensitive flags are ignored, whatever the switches above are set to. Add someone from the
settings.content.trusted.empty: Nobody yet. Trusting an account is useful for someone whose posts are routinely warned but never something you need warning about.

settings.privacy.analytics.hint: Anonymous page counts only — which kinds of page get used, never which account, post or tag you looked at, and never a query string. Turn this off and the analytics script is never loaded at all: nothing is fetched, counted or sent. The script is served from this site, not from a third party. This one is stored in your browser, so there is nothing to save and nothing to fail.
settings.privacy.analytics.label: Count my page views

settings.server.findAnother.hint: We’ll check randomly selected servers from the bundled Mastodon directory. Nothing changes until you approve a working server.
settings.server.intro: Choose the Mastodon server used for public timelines, profiles, and searches while you browse anonymously. Your browser-local identity and preferences stay the same.
settings.server.rejects.hint: These are skipped when hunting for a search server, so a second hunt doesn't re-probe the same servers. A server that turns search on later won't be found again until you forget them.
settings.server.search.here: Searches go here. Everything else uses your own server.
settings.server.search.hint: Many servers disable search for logged-out visitors, and practically none will full-text search posts without an account — the best you get is the posts behind a hashtag, and not every server serves those either. Search — and only search — can be sent to one that does.
settings.server.specific.hint: Enter a server domain if you already know where you want to browse.
settings.server.status.degraded: ⚠ Available, but degraded — images will not load
settings.server.title: Server
settings.spotlight.clicks.explain: Clicks are counted here and nowhere else — there is no server to report them to and no request is made. They're here so you can see which of these you actually found useful.
settings.spotlight.intro: The cards in the right rail are house endorsements — our own projects, and things we think are worth your time. Nobody pays for them, no third party is involved, and nothing about you leaves this browser.
settings.spotlight.rotation: Only {{shown}} are shown at a time, and they change every half hour. The donate links further down the rail are not endorsements and stay put.
settings.spotlight.show.hint: Off means none at all, whatever the individual switches below say. Those keep their settings for when you turn it back on.
settings.spotlight.show.label: Show house endorsements in the right rail
settings.spotlight.title: Endorsements
